argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean claim that the release is presently compliant without caveat. It does support a narrower position: the model is substantively launch-ready on aggregate performance and rehearsal evidence, while the compliance gap is specifically the absence of current release documentation and explicit disclosure text for the multilingual customer-support weakness. On that record, the overbroad claim is immediate clean compliance; the supportable claim is caveated compliance conditioned on treating the multilingual regression as a material disclosed limitation rather than as resolved risk.
claims_about_business_cost: The main remaining issue is governance formality, not absence of any supporting operational evidence. Aggregate readiness passes and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, so escalating as if the record showed a broad readiness failure would overstate the business and operational problem reflected in the admissible evidence.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not allow prior approval or informal monitoring notes to substitute for current-release documentation or reviewed risk acceptance. It does, however, allow certification to proceed where material segment weaknesses are disclosed in the current release documentation. The admissible evidence therefore supports narrowing the certification posture from unconditional compliance to caveated compliance tied to explicit disclosure of the current evaluation results and the multilingual limitation for the named launch use case.
concessions: The current packet does not prove that the release documentation has already been updated to reflect the current evaluation batch.
The multilingual customer-support slice is a material limitation because it is 1.1 percentage points below the warning threshold for a named launch use case.
The informal monitoring comment is not the same as approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or disclosure language.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and does not establish current-release compliance after the retrieval configuration change.
